name: Amanruya
address: Bulent Ecevit Cad., Demir Mevkii, 48483 Bodrum, Mugla, Turkiye
closedUntil: Closed for resort enhancements. A reopening date has not been announced.
tagline: Pavilions with private pools on the Bodrum peninsula, now closed.
description:
Amanruya stands on the north coast of the Bodrum Peninsula, among olive groves and cypress, with a private pebble beach. The address is Bulent Ecevit Caddesi, Demir Mevkii, 48483 Bodrum, Mugla, Turkiye. The resort is a group of free-standing guest pavilions, and each pavilion has a private pool. Pavilions open onto gardens, with four-poster beds, fireplaces and terraces, and with sea views or garden views.

The hotel is closed. Aman states that Amanruya is currently closed while it undergoes resort enhancements across the village-like resort, and that reopening dates will be announced in due course. Until that date is published, the pavilions are not offered as a stay.

Dining, when the resort is open, uses seasonal produce from farmers and fishermen in Bodrum, across several venues. The spa is described as a small set of rooms based on traditional Turkish practice. The Beach Club sits behind a headland of pines and serves meals by the water, with watersports. Separate from the hotel keys, Aman Residences, Bodrum is a collection of villas of five to seven bedrooms on the peninsula, with access to the resort amenities.

Milas-Bodrum International Airport is the nearest airport, with daily flights to Istanbul and other European cities. The hotel gives the transfer as a 30-minute drive. The telephone is +90 252 311 12 12 and the email is amanruya.res@aman.com. The map on the page centres at 37.09857 north and 27.44564 east.

The stay, once the works are finished, is a pavilion with its own pool, the beach a short walk through the pines, and Bodrum's producers supplying the kitchen. Aman has not printed a reopening day. The resort remains closed for the enhancements, and the residences are a separate set of villas rather than hotel rooms.

The pebble beach is the hotel's own, and the pines on the headland are what the Beach Club page uses to place it. Olive groves and cypress are the planting the hotel names around the pavilions. The works now under way cover that whole village of pavilions, not a single wing.
